name: the Oosterplantsoen
title: Ancient Trees in the Oosterplantsoen, Hoorn: 7 to Find
meta_description: Two London planes of the same species, planted twenty years apart in one Hoorn park: one perfect, one squeezed by the kerb. Seven trees along the water.
intro:
Two planes in this park are the same species and the older one is in worse shape, which comes down to where somebody put them. The plane on the Pakhuisstraat went in around 1870 and the town's register notes its base being squeezed by the pavement; the one a couple of hundred metres behind the aviary went in around 1890, out of the way of the street, and the register calls it a perfect tree. Both are over four metres round.

Seven of the trees we map stand here, along the Oosterpoortsgracht and around the Veliusbrug, most of them planted between 1860 and 1910 when the town laid out the strip. Several carry recorded problems, fungal infections at the root collar on two silver maples among them, which the register logs and the town keeps watching. Hoorn signposts its own tree route through the park. It is free and open daily.
